blocks.headline: Der Kalender der Familie Dobart
blocks.bodyGerman:
Hannes ist von Sonntag bis Dienstag in Hamburg.
Mara arbeitet von neun bis siebzehn Uhr.
Florian hat am Samstag ein Spiel.
Lena hat am Montag Geigenunterricht.
Mara trifft am Freitag Annalisa.
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Hannes is in Hamburg from Sunday to Tuesday.
Mara works from 9:00 to 17:00.
Florian has a game on Saturday.
Lena has violin lessons on Monday.
Mara meets Annalisa on Friday.

blocks.ruleHeadline: am + Tag · um + Uhrzeit · von … bis + Zeitraum
blocks.explanationEnglish:
German uses three prepositions for time ideas.
»am« marks a day: am Montag, am Samstag, am Wochenende.
»am« is short for »an + dem«, so it never changes.
»um« marks a clock time: um drei Uhr, um zehn nach neun.
»von … bis« marks a period: von neun bis siebzehn Uhr.
Trap: English says »on Monday« — German needs only »am«, never »an Montag«.
blocks.englishBridge: In English you say on, at and from … to — German uses one word per time idea.
blocks.targetSentenceGerman: Mara arbeitet von neun bis siebzehn Uhr.

examples.german: Florian hat am Samstag ein Spiel.
examples.english: Florian has a game on Saturday.

blocks.headline: Die Familie
blocks.bodyEnglish:
These words name the people in a family.
Learn each noun with its article: der, die or das.

blocks.ruleHeadline: Familienwörter: der, die, das — und der Plural
blocks.explanationEnglish:
Every German noun has an article: der, die or das.
Learn each family word together with its article.
All nouns start with a big letter: der Vater, die Mutter.
Many family plurals add -er and an umlaut: die Väter, die Brüder.
Other plurals add -n or -er without umlaut: die Schwestern, die Kinder.
Trap: English has one word for »the« — German has three articles.
blocks.englishBridge: English uses one word for »the« — German must choose der, die or das.

blocks.headline: Possessivartikel: mein, meine
blocks.bodyGerman: Mein Vater heißt Hannes. Meine Mutter ist Ärztin.
blocks.bodyEnglish:
A possessive article shows who owns something.
It works exactly like an article: der Vater → mein Vater.

blocks.ruleHeadline: mein, dein, sein, ihr — der Possessivartikel
blocks.explanationEnglish:
A possessive article replaces the article and shows the owner.
The owners: ich → mein, du → dein, er/es → sein, sie → ihr, wir → unser.
It changes like an article: der Vater → mein Vater, die Mutter → meine Mutter.
After »besuchen« the noun is accusative, so masculine adds -en: meinen Bruder.
Trap: English »my« never changes — German »mein« becomes »meine« or »meinen«.
blocks.englishBridge: English says my, your, his only once — German changes the word like an article.

blocks.headline: Das »r« am Wortende
blocks.bodyGerman:
Vater [ˈfaːtɐ] · Uhr [ˈuːɐ̯] · Computer [kɔmˈpuːtɐ]
Büro [byˈʁoː] · krank [kʁaŋk] · Schwester [ˈʃvɛstɐ]
blocks.bodyEnglish: In the words »Vater«, »Uhr« and »Computer« the last -r is soft. Say it like the 'a' in 'about'. In »Büro« the r is not last. Then say it soft in the back of the mouth.

vocabHighlight.english: -er at the end of a word

blocks.promptEnglish: Write: My father is called Hannes and my sister lives in Kiel.

blocks.prompt: Match the German family word to the English meaning:
blocks.explanationEnglish: Family nouns keep their article. Learn the article with the noun: der Vater, die Mutter.

items.sentence: Ich habe zwei Kinder. ___ Kinder gehen in die Schule.
Hannes ist ___ Sonntag bis Dienstag in Hamburg.

blocks.explanationEnglish: »Kinder« is plural, so use »Meine«. »Sohn« is masculine, so use »Mein«. Days take »am«, periods take »von … bis«.
The verb »besuchen« takes the accusative. Masculine »der Bruder« becomes »meinen Bruder«.

concept.title: Possessivartikel im Akkusativ
concept.rule: After »besuchen« the noun is accusative. Masculine nouns add -en: mein Vater → meinen Vater.
